dorsal_lateral_high_contrast_texture_top.macro_annuli_edge_geometry: Visible in the lower-lateral region are three distinct 'O'-shaped structures and one irregular 'C'-shaped structure. These features exhibit high-intensity, light-colored perimeters with sharp internal gradients transitioning abruptly into low-intensity darker interiors. The outer edges are roughly 5-10 pixels wide with maximum contrast observed on the dorsal-facing perimeters.
dorsal_lateral_high_contrast_texture_top.high_intensity_blob_density: A high spatial density of small, irregular, high-intensity white blobs is clustered in the anterior-dorsal region, specifically behind the neck. These clusters have high core pixel concentrations with no internal gradient, ranging from 3 to 15 pixels in diameter.
dorsal_lateral_high_contrast_texture_top.constellation_keypoints: The centroids of the three largest 'O' shaped macro-annuli in the lower-lateral region form an obtuse scalene triangle. A secondary cluster of high-intensity blobs near the anterior region forms a dense, irregular polygon when connected to the most dorsal-lateral macro-annulus.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Several circular, depigmented markings representing focal surface trauma or lesions are present on the lower lateral surface. Faint, parallel linear striations are visible on the posterior-dorsal ridge.
